Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old man with 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, headache and chills; no dyspnoea or wheeze.  
- Video inspection shows mild pharyngeal erythema; impression of uncomplicated viral URTI. Symptomatic OTC treatment advised; monitor for deterioration.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection
- Onset: ~5 days ago at start of weekend.
- Symptoms: Dry hacking cough, runny nose, muscle aches, intermittent headaches, chills. No sputum, no haemoptysis, no shortness of breath, no wheeze.
- Exam (video): Mild posterior pharyngeal redness; no tonsillar enlargement; patient palpates no cervical lymphadenopathy.
- Plan: Reassurance; advise Night Nurse/Day Nurse as tolerated with current meds. Red-flag advice—seek review if SOB, wheeze, or symptoms >3 weeks.

Issue 2: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
- Diagnosed 5–6 years ago.
- Home glucose monitoring: “No issues, nothing out of the ordinary.”
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No acute concerns raised today.

Issue 3: Hypertension
- Described as “slight blood pressure.”
- On lisinopril; last home BP reading this morning “within normal range” (exact value not recalled).
- No current symptoms of uncontrolled BP.

Medications:
- Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol (as needed) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- OTC recommendation given: Night Nurse / Day Nurse (cold remedy).

Allergies:
- Not discussed / not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus (5–6 years).  
- Hypertension.

Social History:
- Not discussed.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed (cervical screening, mammogram, prostate PSA, FOBT, BMD, vaccinations, optometry, skin check—all not documented).

Physical Examination:
- Video assessment: Mild erythematous pharynx, no tonsillar hypertrophy, no palpable cervical nodes (by patient report).
- No vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Symptomatic treatment with Night Nurse/Day Nurse; continue paracetamol prn.
- Continue regular metformin and lisinopril.
- Safety-net: Contact healthcare provider if shortness of breath, wheeze, or symptoms persist >3 weeks or worsen.
- No prescription required today.
- Routine diabetes and BP reviews to continue with usual care team.
